sentences.zh: 他们问，你愿意担任财政部长吗？

sentences.zh: 他干了五天，然后坐火车回到了科英布拉，他说，你们不让我做我想做的事，也就是削减开支和进行所有这些改革。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想干了。

sentences.zh: 他们不断把他拉回来，说，当财政部长，把账目理顺。

sentences.zh: 而他不断威胁要辞职。

sentences.zh: 每次他威胁辞职，他们基本上就给他更多的权力。

sentences.zh: 所以到了1928年，他成了财政部长，可以说是永久性的。

sentences.zh: 所以你基本上可以从财政部管理整个政府。

sentences.zh: 到了1932年，他成了总理。

sentences.zh: 说真的，当我提到总理时，我的意思是，他基本上就是政府本身。

sentences.zh: 所以其他人都要听他的。

sentences.en: Well, he has almost quasi-dictatorial power, even though he's only prime minister, not president.

sentences.en: And he's only prime minister for the whole, all the decades that he's in control in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 而且在他在葡萄牙掌权的几十年里，他一直都只是总理。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's never president.
sentences.zh: 是的，他从未担任过总统。

sentences.en: He's always prime minister serving at the discretion of the president.
sentences.zh: 他始终是以总理身份，听命于总统。

sentences.en: So how is he maintaining power?
sentences.zh: 那么他是如何维持权力的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what are the underpinnings, the kind of, the practical underpinnings?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有什么基础，那种实际的基础？

sentences.en: The practical underpinnings are he does sort out the economy.
sentences.zh: 实际的基础是他确实理顺了经济。

sentences.en: So he does sort out Portugal's debt.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实解决了葡萄牙的债务问题。

sentences.en: And he starts running balanced budgets.
sentences.zh: 他开始实行平衡预算。

sentences.en: Um, they've had incredible turbulence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们之前经历了难以置信的动荡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they recognize that he is an incredibly clever and hardworking man of this kind of flinty, slightly terrifying integrity.
sentences.zh: 他们认识到他是一个极其聪明和勤奋的人，有着那种坚毅、略带恐怖的正直感。

sentences.en: Uh, he also has an enormous appeal to Catholic, middle-class conservatives.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他对天主教中产阶级保守派也有巨大的吸引力。

sentences.en: And of course, he's a very useful tool for the big landowners, for the army, for the Catholic Church, because they have found somebody who is exceedingly competent,
sentences.zh: 当然，对于大土地所有者、军队和天主教会来说，他是一个非常有用的工具，因为他们找到了一个极其能干的人，

sentences.en: who will protect their interests from socialism, Bolshevism, anarchism, you know, who will, who will, and his thing is, he freezes in place the status quo.
sentences.zh: 他会保护他们的利益免受社会主义、布尔什维克主义、无政府主义的侵害，你知道，他所做的就是将现状冻结在原地。

sentences.en: But what I'm trying to understand is the degree to which he is a dictator, or whether,
sentences.zh: 但我试图理解的是，他在多大程度上是一个独裁者，或者说，

sentences.zh: 他的权力地位是否取决于他拥有国家内部强大集团的支持。

sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这大概适用于所有独裁者，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: That they actually, the fantasy that we have, which is that they're bond villains.

sentences.en: Well, no, because Hitler is a Führer.

sentences.en: I mean, they indisputably stand at the head of the state, and they have a kind of, they claim a heroic status by virtue of that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们无可争议地站在国家元首的位置上，并且凭借这一点，他们声称拥有某种英雄地位。

sentences.en: I mean, if Salazar is just the prime minister, you know, he's not even the president, then that is, that is quite a difference, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果萨拉查只是总理，你知道，他甚至不是总统，那么这确实有很大的不同，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is what makes him, Tom, such a richly fascinating study, because, as you say, he appears to be in many ways, I mean, you make the comparisons with Hitler and Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是为什么他是一个如此引人入胜的研究对象，因为正如你所说，他在许多方面看起来，我的意思是，你把他与希特勒和墨索里尼进行了比较。

sentences.zh: 他只是总理。

sentences.zh: 他不举行集会。

sentences.zh: 他没有集会。

sentences.zh: 他没有个人崇拜。

sentences.zh: 他实际上没有政党。

sentences.zh: 所以他们有了一部新宪法，一部法团主义宪法。

sentences.zh: 他有一个单一政党，国民联盟，他基本上将其作为非政党来推销。

sentences.en: He has no interest in mobilizing the masses.
sentences.zh: 他对动员群众毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: He doesn't really sell himself as anything other than a technocrat, so the public, sort of Catholic technocrat.
sentences.zh: 他并不真的把自己推销为除技术官僚以外的任何东西，所以公众，某种天主教技术官僚。

sentences.en: There's no sense of energizing young people.
sentences.zh: 没有那种激励年轻人的感觉。

sentences.en: There's no sense of embracing modernity, of military expansion, of all these other aspects of the sort of...
sentences.zh: 没有那种拥抱现代性、军事扩张的感觉，没有那种……

sentences.en: The hyperactive, the hysterical side of 1920s fascism, he has none of that.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代法西斯主义那种过度活跃、歇斯底里的一面，他一点都没有。

sentences.en: So on his propaganda posters, he portrays himself as figures from the Portugal to the right paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以在他宣传海报上，他把自己描绘成葡萄牙过去的人物。

sentences.en: So he compares himself to John Abraganza, Jawa Abraganza.
sentences.zh: 所以他把自己比作布拉干萨的约翰，若昂·德·布拉干萨。

sentences.en: He does indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And actually, so the great historian of fascism, Robert Paxton, says that one of the confusing things about Salazar is that Salazar,
sentences.zh: 事实上，法西斯主义的伟大历史学家罗伯特·帕克斯顿说，关于萨拉查令人困惑的事情之一是，萨拉查，

sentences.en: he copies often the language and the iconography, which is so common in the 1920s and 30s, of fascism.
sentences.zh: 他经常抄袭20世纪20和30年代法西斯主义中非常常见的语言和肖像。

sentences.en: So you see a Salazarist monument or you see a Salazarist poster, and they do look very fascistic.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到萨拉查主义的纪念碑或海报，它们看起来确实非常法西斯化。

sentences.en: But the difference is that there has none of the dynamism or the excitement or the radicalism that fascism holds out, which is so intoxicating to younger voters often in the 20s.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，他没有法西斯主义所具有的任何活力、兴奋或激进主义，而这些在20年代往往让年轻选民感到陶醉。

sentences.en: So in Mussolini's Italy, let's say.
sentences.zh: 比如在墨索里尼的意大利。

sentences.zh: 萨拉查试图做的一切，都是一个相当去个人化的政权。

sentences.zh: 所以呈现给公众的他的形象是这种……

sentences.en: He's very frugal.
sentences.zh: 他非常节俭。

sentences.en: He's unmarried.
sentences.zh: 他未婚。

sentences.zh: 他不喜欢权力的排场。

sentences.zh: 是的，他有点像僧侣。

sentences.en: Monkish, exactly.
sentences.zh: 像僧侣，没错。

sentences.en: An academic, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上是一位学者。

sentences.en: And people often say he governs like a professor.
sentences.zh: 人们常说他像教授一样治理国家。

sentences.en: He works all the time in his office.
sentences.zh: 他一直在办公室工作。

sentences.en: He doesn't believe in the heating because he thinks it's wasteful.
sentences.zh: 他不相信供暖，因为他认为那是浪费。

sentences.en: Or like a schoolteacher, a teacher treating the Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 或者像个学校老师，一个把葡萄牙人当作孩子的老师。

sentences.en: Portuguese as children.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人当作孩子。

sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我正想说，你很享受这个。

sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在上一个播客里谈到了那个不肯脱外套的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dom Zhao.

sentences.zh: 所以他穿着大衣工作。

sentences.en: Well, a model there for everyone in Europe.

sentences.zh: 这只会……

sentences.zh: 那根本不是什么口号。

sentences.en: But so if he's a schoolteacher, schoolteachers have the right to punish their pupils, their students.
sentences.zh: 但如果他是个学校老师，学校老师有权惩罚他们的学生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 那么萨拉查行使的控制机构是什么？

sentences.zh: 有一个秘密警察。

sentences.en: It goes through various incarnations.
sentences.zh: 它经历了各种化身。

sentences.en: It's best known as the PIDE.
sentences.zh: 它最广为人知的是PIDE。

sentences.en: And they have prisons.
sentences.zh: 他们有监狱。

sentences.en: They have...

sentences.zh: 他们有集中营吗？

sentences.en: For dissidents.
sentences.zh: 为了异见人士。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，休息后我们会谈到二战后对异见人士的一些镇压。

sentences.zh: 但他们确实……

sentences.zh: 人们确实会死亡，人们确实会失踪。

sentences.zh: 萨拉查之所以受到如此多的争论，在某种程度上，他看起来是一个如此模棱两可的人物，原因之一是，一方面，人们失踪并死亡。

sentences.zh: 另一方面，与20世纪其他社会相比，人数并不多。

sentences.en: So I found it...
sentences.zh: 所以我发现……

sentences.en: Over...
sentences.zh: 超过……

sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是从20世纪20年代中期到1968年、1970年。

sentences.zh: 所以那是一段很长的时间。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以说每年有一两个人被秘密警察在监狱里折磨致死、殴打，或者被他的秘密警察弄失踪。

sentences.zh: 但葡萄牙没有死刑。

sentences.zh: 而且他没有重新引入它。

sentences.zh: 不，他没有重新引入它。

sentences.zh: 所以他拥有所谓的“新国家”，他的新国家。

sentences.en: Again, you know, that's very, very 20s, 30s kind of dictatorship, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 同样，你知道，那是20、30年代那种非常典型的独裁统治，不是吗？

sentences.en: To talk of a new state.
sentences.zh: 谈论一个新国家。

sentences.zh: 但他与墨索里尼或希特勒的新国家的区别在于，他不想带领葡萄牙进入一个新时代。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一个很棒的故事，很久以后，我想是在60年代，当有人告诉他安哥拉发现了石油时，

sentences.en: If Salazar is a devout Catholic, what is his attitude to the kind of the pagan strain, say, within Nazism?

sentences.zh: 好吧，我不太知道该怎么看待这一点。

sentences.en: So Salazar does think that Nazis are pagan.
sentences.zh: 所以萨拉查确实认为纳粹是异教徒。

sentences.en: So he's a very, very reactionary Catholic.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个非常、非常反动的天主教徒。

sentences.en: And he hates Bolshevism, socialism, all of this stuff, which he sees as godless and evil.
sentences.zh: 他憎恨布尔什维主义、社会主义以及所有这些东西，他认为这些是无神论和邪恶的。

sentences.en: So from that point of view, he sees the fascists as, I suppose, a useful bulwark against it.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度来看，我想他把法西斯分子视为抵御这些东西的有用堡垒。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, he says, he describes Hitler and the Nazis as, he says, they are pagan.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，他说，他形容希特勒和纳粹，他说，他们是异教徒。

sentences.en: They're incompatible with the character of our Christian civilization.
sentences.zh: 他们与我们基督教文明的特征不相容。

sentences.en: There are attempts to have kind of overtly fascist movements in Portugal, as there are in every other European country.
sentences.zh: 在葡萄牙，像在其他每个欧洲国家一样，也有人试图建立公开的法西斯运动。

sentences.en: In Portugal, it's a group called the Blue Shirts.
sentences.zh: 在葡萄牙，这是一个叫“蓝衫党”的组织。

sentences.en: Salazar basically purges them, denounces them.
sentences.zh: 萨拉查基本上清洗了他们，谴责了他们。

sentences.en: He condemns, and it's interesting, he condemns what he calls the exaltation of youth, the cult of force through direct action,
sentences.zh: 他谴责，有趣的是，他谴责他所说的对青年的崇拜，通过直接行动进行的武力崇拜，

sentences.en: the principle of the superiority of state political power and social life, and the propensity for organizing masses behind a single leader.
sentences.zh: 以及国家政治权力和社会生活至上的原则，还有在单一领导人背后组织群众的倾向。

sentences.en: I mean, that's actually a pretty good, you know, academic definition of fascism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这实际上是一个相当不错的、你知道的，关于法西斯的学术定义。

sentences.en: And he basically says, all of that is bad.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，所有这些都是坏的。

sentences.en: He very much sounds like the kind of chap who would not be in favor of the exaltation of youth.
sentences.zh: 他听起来确实像那种不会赞成崇拜青年的人。

sentences.en: Definitely not a man for the exaltation of youth, no.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是一个崇拜青年的人，没错。

sentences.zh: 他身上有什么雅各布·里斯-莫格的影子吗？

sentences.zh: 不，我不觉得。

sentences.en: Well, maybe I'm revealing too much about my opinion of Jacob Rees-Mogg.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我对自己对雅各布·里斯-莫格的看法透露得太多了。

sentences.en: But I don't think there's anything at all contrived about.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他身上一点也不做作。

sentences.en: So Jacob Rees-Mogg loves the media, and he loves to appear on the media.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·里斯-莫格喜欢媒体，他喜欢在媒体上露面。

sentences.zh: 而且他的人设经过非常精心的设计，你知道，为了获得曝光度。

sentences.zh: 萨拉查讨厌曝光。

sentences.zh: 他确实像个僧侣。

sentences.en: He's very austere.
sentences.zh: 他非常简朴。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 而且他不富有。

sentences.en: No, he's not.
sentences.zh: 不，他不是。

sentences.en: Well, he's, I mean, he's not badly off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他并不穷。

sentences.en: I mean, he has a summer house, and he has his residence and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有避暑别墅，有住所之类的。

sentences.en: But is he corrupt?
sentences.zh: 但他腐败吗？

sentences.en: He's not corrupt.
sentences.zh: 他不腐败。

sentences.en: He's not.
sentences.zh: 他不是。

sentences.en: No, I don't think he is especially corrupt, actually.
sentences.zh: 不，我其实不认为他特别腐败。

sentences.en: I mean, he's definitely, he works with people who are corrupt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他确实与腐败的人共事。

sentences.en: And you could, like all dictatorships, his regime has plenty of corruption.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以说，像所有独裁政权一样，他的政权有很多腐败。

sentences.en: But personally, he lives with this, I mean, this extraordinary personal life.
sentences.zh: 但就个人而言，他过着这种，我的意思是，这种非凡的个人生活。

sentences.en: So he works all the time.
sentences.zh: 他一直在工作。

sentences.en: Life magazine said, I mean, very insulting to the Portuguese, actually, this, the American magazine Life said of him, he is everything that most Portuguese are not.
sentences.zh: 《生活》杂志说，实际上对葡萄牙人非常侮辱，这家美国杂志说他：他拥有大多数葡萄牙人所没有的一切。

sentences.en: Calm, silent, ascetic, puritanical, a glutton for work, cool to women.
sentences.zh: 冷静、沉默、禁欲、清教徒式、工作狂、对女性冷淡。

sentences.zh: 但他和这位叫唐娜·玛丽亚的管家住在一起。

sentences.zh: 她算是一个农民。

sentences.en: She was initially a sort of illiterate sort of servant woman who basically stays with him as his housekeeper.
sentences.zh: 她最初是一个文盲式的女仆，基本上作为管家留在他身边。

sentences.en: Is that in inverted commas, housekeeper?
sentences.zh: 那个“管家”是加了引号的吗？

sentences.zh: 嗯，人们说，他有这样一个同居伴侣难道不神秘吗？

sentences.en: And she had two nieces that he was very kind to.
sentences.zh: 她有两个侄女，他对她们非常好。

sentences.zh: 所以他的一些葡萄牙反对者说，哦，这些显然是他的孩子。

sentences.en: I don't think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是真的。

sentences.en: An extraordinary thing that when she died in 1981, so 11 years after Salazar, the director of the care home where she had been living decided that for the sake of her reputation,

sentences.zh: 他要让人检查她是否还是处女。

sentences.zh: 显然她是。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 但另一个比较是，我的意思是，让我们陈述一下这个比较，不仅是与希特勒，还有与墨索里尼和佛朗哥的比较。

sentences.en: Mussolini is all about strutting.

sentences.en: It's about pomposity.
sentences.zh: 关于浮夸。

sentences.en: It's about display and swagger and sort of this sort of almost comical kind of virility.
sentences.zh: 关于展示、摆架子，以及那种近乎滑稽的男子气概。

sentences.en: Salazar, it's inconceivable.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，佛朗哥是一个非常令人讨厌的人。

sentences.en: Salazar can't really stand Franco.
sentences.zh: 萨拉查真的受不了佛朗哥。

sentences.en: Franco is a great show off.
sentences.zh: 佛朗哥是个大显摆。

sentences.en: He's all about, you know, he's lots of medals, lots of pomp, lots of display.
sentences.zh: 他的一切都是，你知道，他有很多勋章，很多排场，很多展示。

sentences.en: His family become incredibly rich.
sentences.zh: 他的家人变得极其富有。

sentences.en: Again, Salazar has none of this.
sentences.zh: 同样，萨拉查没有这些。

sentences.en: So one of the things that I suppose makes him almost uncomfortable to study is that in some ways, he's the kind of person that when we're writing about political leaders,
sentences.zh: 所以我想让他变得难以研究的原因之一是，在某些方面，他正是那种我们在写政治领导人时，

sentences.zh: 往往会忍不住觉得相当令人钦佩，虽然是以一种冷冰冰的方式，因为他确实有这种严肃性和正直感。

sentences.en: But of course, he is running a very repressive, incredibly reactionary regime in which you, you know, the free speech is limited.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他经营着一个非常压抑、极其反动的政权，在那里，你知道，言论自由受到限制。

sentences.en: The newspapers, there's huge censorship and political dissidents are jailed, if not tortured.
sentences.zh: 报纸有严格的审查制度，政治异见人士被监禁，甚至遭受酷刑。

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose you could put it this way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想你可以这样说。

sentences.zh: 如果你可以选择在30年代和40年代在意大利、西班牙、

sentences.zh: 是的，你会的。

sentences.zh: 我相信你会的。

sentences.en: I'm sure you would.
sentences.zh: 我相信你会的。

sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一个有趣的问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: So given where Portugal is, it's on the European periphery, given its economic and political condition,
sentences.zh: 考虑到葡萄牙所处的位置，它在欧洲边缘，考虑到它的经济和政治状况，

sentences.en: which is analogous to Spain, maybe Italy or Greece, I suppose, or indeed countries of Latin America.
sentences.zh: 这与西班牙，也许是意大利或希腊，或者确实是拉丁美洲国家类似。

sentences.en: I mean, Portugal is terribly sleepy and stagnant in the middle of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，20世纪中叶的葡萄牙非常沉睡和停滞。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, it doesn't have coups.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你知道，它没有政变。

sentences.en: It doesn't have a civil war.
sentences.zh: 它没有内战。

sentences.en: It doesn't have mass repression, mass terror, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 它没有大规模镇压、大规模恐怖，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: So, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道。

sentences.en: Best of a bad lot.
sentences.zh: 烂苹果里挑好的。

sentences.en: Maybe the best of a bad job.

sentences.en: Or, I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 或者，我的意思是，谁知道呢？

sentences.zh: 萨拉查的替代者可能不是。

sentences.en: It was a civil war, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜会是一场内战。

sentences.en: A happy, successful democracy.
sentences.zh: 一个幸福、成功的民主国家。

sentences.en: It might well have been, yeah, more bombings, more terrorism, more.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，是的，更多的爆炸，更多的恐怖主义，更多。

sentences.en: And he keeps Portugal out of the Second World War?
sentences.zh: 而且他让葡萄牙远离了第二次世界大战？

sentences.en: So it's basically a peninsular war all over again.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上又是一场半岛战争。

sentences.en: So Salazar is sort of relatively benevolently disposed towards the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 所以萨拉查对纳粹的态度相对来说还算比较友善。

sentences.en: He's not, you know, by the standards of people's attitudes to the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以当时人们对纳粹的态度来看，他其实并不是这样。

sentences.en: You know, he's so anti-communist that in some ways they could be natural allies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他非常反共，在某些方面他们甚至可能是天然的盟友。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, of course, Britain is all important.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，当然，英国至关重要。

sentences.zh: 所以即使在19世纪和20世纪初，英国仍然占据了葡萄牙进口额的很大一部分，我想大概有四分之一左右。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's a dominating kind of economic factor.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一种主导性的经济因素。

sentences.en: So he can't alienate the British, but also he's terrified of alienating the Germans.
sentences.zh: 所以他不能疏远英国人，但他同时也非常害怕疏远德国人。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to jump into bed with the British because he thinks Lisbon will be bombed and, you know, Portuguese bases will be bombed and so on.
sentences.zh: 他不想和英国人搅在一起，因为他认为里斯本会被轰炸，你知道，葡萄牙的基地也会被轰炸等等。

sentences.en: So basically, right at the beginning, he squares it with the British.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，从一开始，他就和英国人达成了共识。

sentences.en: He says, you know, we're still your allies, but we're going to remain neutral in this war.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我们仍然是你们的盟友，但我们将在这场战争中保持中立。

sentences.en: And the British are completely fine with that.
sentences.zh: 而英国人对此完全没意见。

sentences.en: They understand that and they actually confirm that.
sentences.zh: 他们理解这一点，并且实际上确认了这一点。

sentences.en: They send him a kind of diplomatic note saying that's completely fine.

sentences.en: They're finalists three times.
sentences.zh: 他们三次进入决赛。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, the heyday of Eusebio.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是尤西比奥的全盛时期。

sentences.en: And Eusebio, he is probably the single most internationally famous Portuguese person before Cristiano Ronaldo.
sentences.zh: 尤西比奥大概是克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多之前，在国际上最著名的葡萄牙人。

sentences.zh: 以他的教会史研究和君士坦丁传记而闻名。

sentences.en: Well, Eusebio is interesting because, of course, he's black.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尤西比奥很有趣，因为他当然是黑人。

sentences.zh: 他出生在莫桑比克的一个非常贫穷的家庭。

sentences.en: And what I think is fascinating about Eusebio is Eusebio becomes this international avatar of Portugal at a point at which Portugal's relationship with those colonies,
sentences.zh: 我认为尤西比奥最迷人的地方在于，他成为了葡萄牙的国际化身，而当时葡萄牙与那些殖民地，

sentences.en: with Mozambique, with Angola, is increasingly strained.
sentences.zh: 与莫桑比克、安哥拉的关系正日益紧张。

sentences.en: So, as we said, they'd always said they're not an empire.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们所说，他们一直宣称自己不是帝国。

sentences.en: We're a pluricontinental nation.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个跨大陆的国家。

sentences.en: But obviously, by the mid-1960s, you know.
sentences.zh: 但显然，到了20世纪60年代中期，你知道。

sentences.zh: 嗯，他们失去了果阿，不是吗？

sentences.en: So there's a brilliant story about that, that the Indian Army was kind of, you know, moving in on Goa and there who sends the tanks in.
sentences.zh: 关于这件事有个精彩的故事，当时印度军队正准备进入果阿，是谁派坦克进去的呢。

sentences.en: And the military authorities in Goa send a telegram to the general staff in Lisbon requesting sausages.
sentences.zh: 果阿的军事当局向里斯本的总参谋部发了一封电报，请求提供“香肠”。

sentences.en: And sausages is code for cannon shells.
sentences.zh: 而“香肠”是炮弹的代号。

sentences.en: And the general staff sent a whole batch of pork sausages.
sentences.zh: 结果总参谋部真的发了一大批猪肉香肠过去。

sentences.en: To actually send them sausages?
sentences.zh: 真的给他们发了香肠？

sentences.en: They literally sent them sausages because they'd forgotten that this was the code.
sentences.zh: 他们真的发了香肠，因为他们忘了这是代号。

sentences.en: So Goa falls to become part of India again.
sentences.zh: 所以果阿沦陷，重新成为了印度的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And by the late 1960s, there have been uprisings in Angola and Mozambique in what becomes Guinea-Bissau.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪60年代末，安哥拉、莫桑比克和后来成为几内亚比绍的地方都爆发了起义。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Portuguese are very dependent on, they're still dependent actually on Britain and on the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，葡萄牙人非常依赖，实际上他们仍然依赖英国和美国。

sentences.en: Salazar is becoming boxed in.
sentences.zh: 萨拉查正陷入困境。

sentences.en: He's becoming increasingly, you know, his friends are South Africa and Rhodesia.
sentences.zh: 他越来越，你知道，他的朋友只有南非和罗得西亚。

sentences.en: So the breakaway regime in Rhodesia.
sentences.zh: 也就是罗得西亚那个分裂政权。

sentences.en: And he's sort of supporting the Ian Smith regime in Rhodesia.
sentences.zh: 他在某种程度上支持罗得西亚的伊恩·史密斯政权。

sentences.en: So actually Mozambique becomes one of the world's most important kind of trading centers because all Rhodesian trade has to be funneled through Mozambique to break the boycott.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上莫桑比克成为了世界上最重要的贸易中心之一，因为所有罗得西亚的贸易都必须通过莫桑比克来打破抵制。

sentences.en: But, you know, the spending on the army to try and fight off the sort of nationalist uprisings in Africa is absorbing more and more of the Portuguese budget.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，为了抵御非洲的民族主义起义，在军队上的开支正消耗着越来越多的葡萄牙预算。

sentences.en: So in total, 8,000.
So the same is similar to the First World War, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以这和第一次世界大战很像，汤姆。

sentences.en: About 8,000 Portuguese are killed fighting in Angola and Mozambique in the late 60s.
sentences.zh: 在60年代末，大约有8000名葡萄牙人在安哥拉和莫桑比克的战斗中阵亡。

sentences.en: And presumably the Portuguese economy is still very much flatlining at this point.
sentences.zh: 而且大概葡萄牙经济在这一点上仍然处于停滞状态。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, well, it's grown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，嗯，它增长了。

sentences.en: So all Western European economies have grown after the World War II.
sentences.zh: 二战后所有西欧经济体都增长了。

sentences.en: So Salazar's defenders will often say, look, look how much Portugal's economy grew in the 1940s, 1950s, 1960s.
sentences.zh: 所以萨拉查的辩护者经常会说，看，看看葡萄牙经济在40、50、60年代增长了多少。

sentences.en: I think the truth probably is that whoever, you know, Mickey Mouse could have been Prime Minister of Portugal and it would have grown.
sentences.zh: 我认为事实可能是，无论谁，你知道，哪怕是米老鼠当葡萄牙总理，经济也会增长。

sentences.en: But you're right, Portugal's economy is still, it is still the poorest country in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的，葡萄牙经济仍然是西欧最贫穷的。

sentences.en: It can ill afford these African wars.
sentences.zh: 它根本负担不起这些非洲战争。

sentences.en: And there's a definite sense, I think, by the late 1960s that this guy who was reactionary even by the standards of the 1920s, who's still running the country.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为到60年代末，有一种明确的感觉，这个即便以20年代标准来看都很反动的人，依然在统治着这个国家。

sentences.en: So he's still running the country in 1968.
sentences.zh: 所以他在1968年还在统治国家。

sentences.en: So there's soissons we tar out on the streets and the hair is long and the jostics are burning.
sentences.zh: 当时街头到处是抗议，人们留着长发，烧着香。

sentences.en: And he's fulminating against Martin Luther.
sentences.zh: 而他还在抨击马丁·路德。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: So what happens to him?
sentences.zh: 那他后来怎么了？

sentences.en: He's at his house, his sort of summer residence.
sentences.zh: 他在他的房子里，也就是他的避暑别墅。

sentences.en: There are different accounts, but I think the most likely thing is he falls off his chair.
sentences.zh: 有不同的说法，但我认为最可能的情况是他从椅子上摔了下来。

sentences.en: Some people say it's in the bath, but I think it's his chair.
sentences.zh: 有些人说是洗澡时摔的，但我认为是椅子。

sentences.en: On the 3rd of August, 1968, and he suffers a brain hemorrhage.
sentences.zh: 1968年8月3日，他患上了脑溢血。

sentences.en: He appears to get better.
sentences.zh: 他看起来好转了。

sentences.en: But after two weeks, he goes into a massive decline.
sentences.zh: 但两周后，他的病情急剧恶化。

sentences.en: He goes into hospital.
sentences.zh: 他进了医院。

sentences.en: He goes into a coma.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了昏迷。

sentences.en: However, the president, who's sort of one of these identikit, slightly faceless kind of military conservative types, he thinks Salazar must be about to die.
sentences.zh: 然而，总统，那种千篇一律、面目模糊的军事保守派类型，他认为萨拉查快要死了。

sentences.en: So he formally dismisses him as prime minister and he gets another academic, actually, the former rector of Lisbon University,
sentences.zh: 于是他正式解除了萨拉查的总理职务，并找了另一位学者，实际上是里斯本大学的前校长，

sentences.en: one of Salazar's old associates called Marcelo Caetano, a very distinguished constitutional lawyer.
sentences.zh: 萨拉查的一位老同事，名叫马塞洛·卡埃塔诺，一位非常杰出的宪法学者。

sentences.en: You know, it's weird that there's this dictatorship of academics, of university professors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种由学者、大学教授组成的独裁统治真是奇怪。

sentences.en: So Caetano becomes prime minister.
sentences.zh: 于是卡埃塔诺成为了总理。

sentences.en: But Salazar doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 但萨拉查并没有死。

sentences.en: He lives for another 23 months and nobody tells him.
sentences.zh: 他又活了23个月，而且没人告诉他。

sentences.en: Is he conscious?
sentences.zh: 他有意识吗？

sentences.en: He's conscious.
sentences.zh: 他有意识。

sentences.en: He's lucid.
sentences.zh: 他神志清醒。

sentences.en: He's been in a coma for, I think, a month.
sentences.zh: 我想他昏迷了大概一个月。

sentences.en: But nobody says you're no longer prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但没人告诉他你已经不再是总理了。

sentences.en: I mean, they basically say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们基本上就这样做了。

sentences.en: So what, he's kind of giving orders and people pretend to obey them?
sentences.zh: 所以，他在下达命令，而人们假装服从？

sentences.en: I think he's in a, I mean, he's obviously not complete, he's 80, he's obviously not, you know, functioning at the peak of dynamism and people are saying to him.
sentences.zh: 我想他处于一种，我的意思是，他显然不完整，他80岁了，显然没有，你知道，处于活力的巅峰，人们在对他说话。

sentences.en: But it's like Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 但这就像乔·拜登一样。

sentences.en: Well, I think Joe Biden is still president, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为乔·拜登还是总统，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, unless things are happening behind the scenes that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除非幕后发生了我们不知道的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I've seen very exaggerated stories about this where people say, oh, the Lisbon newspapers produced fake editions, which were shown to Salazar every day.
sentences.zh: 没错，我的意思是，我见过关于此事的非常夸张的故事，说里斯本的报纸制作了假版本，每天给萨拉查看。

sentences.en: So that he would think he was still prime minister.
sentences.zh: 这样他就会以为自己还是总理。

sentences.en: I find that hard to believe that a newspaper would go to such ludicrous lengths for almost two years.
sentences.zh: 我很难相信一家报纸会为了近两年时间做出如此荒谬的举动。

sentences.en: But I think they didn't tell him he'd been sacked.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们确实没告诉他他已经被解职了。

sentences.en: And, you know, he just thinks that my deputies are doing the work and I'm sort of sitting here at home recuperating.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他只是认为我的副手们在做工作，而我只是坐在家里休养。

sentences.en: And then eventually in 1970, he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后最终在1970年，他去世了。

sentences.en: And the regime, well, we will come back to the fate of the regime.
sentences.zh: 而那个政权，嗯，我们会回到那个政权的命运。

sentences.en: And the last Western European revolution, which takes place in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 以及20世纪70年代发生的最后一场西欧革命。

sentences.en: I think we should come back to that, shouldn't we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该回到那个话题，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yes, as part of this exciting package of projects that we have coming your way in November.
sentences.zh: 是的，作为我们11月即将推出的激动人心的项目组合的一部分。

sentences.en: So we won't say anything more.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就不多说了。

sentences.en: We'll just kind of tantalise you with that.
sentences.zh: 我们只是先吊吊你们的胃口。

sentences.zh: 但我们会回到葡萄牙，把这个故事讲完。

sentences.en: So, Tom, let me ask you just before we wrap up, I'm curious about what you think about Salazar.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，在结束之前我想问你，我很好奇你对萨拉查的看法。

sentences.en: So you're an outsider to this, as it were.
sentences.zh: 你算是这个问题的局外人。

sentences.en: You've not written about Portuguese history.
sentences.zh: 你没有写过关于葡萄牙历史的文章。

sentences.en: But you are obviously really interested in the Catholicism and the political Christianity, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 但你显然对天主教和政治基督教非常感兴趣，我想。

sentences.en: So what's your take on him?
sentences.zh: 所以你对他有什么看法？

sentences.zh: 我很好奇他显然在多大程度上拥有。

sentences.en: He must have had a measure of popular support.
sentences.zh: 他一定拥有一定程度的民众支持。

sentences.en: Because if he, I mean, if his security apparatus, I mean, it sounds repressive, but it's not the Gestapo, is it?
sentences.zh: 因为如果他，我的意思是，如果他的安全机构，听起来很压抑，但那不是盖世太保，对吧？

sentences.en: No, it's grim.
sentences.zh: 不，它很阴森。

sentences.en: And I don't want to downplay it, because there'll be some Portuguese listeners to this.
sentences.zh: 我不想淡化它，因为会有一些葡萄牙听众听到这个。

sentences.en: By and large, the traditional fascist states, they make a virtue of being repressive.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，传统的法西斯国家，他们以压迫为荣。

sentences.en: They rub people's noses in it.
sentences.zh: 他们把这强加给人们。

sentences.en: If he's not doing that, then he must have a measure of support.
sentences.zh: 如果他没有那样做，那么他一定拥有一定程度的支持。

sentences.en: And I guess the fact that 40% vote for him in this poll suggests that it's ongoing.
sentences.zh: 我想在这次民调中40%的人投票给他，这表明这种支持仍在持续。

sentences.en: That is, I guess, unsettling if you're for narratives of liberal, you know, the perspective of democracy and liberalism,
sentences.zh: 如果你支持自由主义的叙事，你知道，民主和自由主义的视角，这确实令人不安，

sentences.en: to imagine that someone who is so reactionary and so clearly repressive could have maintained such popular support for so long.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，一个如此反动且明显压迫的人竟然能维持如此长久的民众支持。

sentences.en: Well, what's interesting is he's become quite fashionable in some circles in recent years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的是，近年来他在某些圈子里变得相当时髦了。

sentences.en: So the magazine, The American Conservative, published a big essay a couple of years ago called Waiting for Salazar,

sentences.en: basically saying, you know, he's the philosopher king, post-liberal age.
sentences.zh: 大意是说，你知道，他是后自由主义时代的哲学王。

sentences.en: But was he a philosopher king?
sentences.zh: 但他真的是哲学王吗？

sentences.en: Dean Acheson, who was the Truman Secretary of State, he described him as the closest thing the 20th century had to a platonic philosopher king.
sentences.zh: 杜鲁门时期的国务卿迪安·艾奇逊曾形容他，称他是20世纪最接近柏拉图式哲学王的人。

sentences.en: I mean, but platonic philosopher kings are famously repressive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但柏拉图式的哲学王可是出了名的压迫者。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, I agree, I think he is an unsettling, it's odd that he's an unsettling figure because he's so ambiguous,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想，我同意，我觉得他是一个令人不安的人物，说他令人不安很奇怪，因为他太模棱两可了，

sentences.en: because there are things about him, the work ethic, the seriousness that...
sentences.zh: 因为他身上有些东西，那种职业道德，那种严肃性……

sentences.en: The thing about fascism, you know who the goodies and the baddies are.
sentences.zh: 关于法西斯主义，你知道谁是好人，谁是坏人。

sentences.en: It's very clear who the baddies are.
sentences.zh: 谁是坏人非常清楚。

sentences.en: I guess Salazar is, I mean, he sounds as if it's a slightly more complicated figure than that, that you can't just 100% engage in the kind of goodies and baddies.
sentences.zh: 我想萨拉查，我的意思是，他听起来是一个比那复杂得多的人物，你不能简单地用那种好人坏人的二元论来衡量他。

sentences.en: That's, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想那是对的。

sentences.en: That's what Tom Gallagher, his biographer says, is that he's much more ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 他的传记作者汤姆·加拉格尔就是这么说的，说他要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And actually, it's very hard to kind of pin him down with a moralistic kind of label.
sentences.zh: 事实上，很难用某种道德标签来定义他。

sentences.en: Anyway...
sentences.zh: 总之……

sentences.en: So he's not raciSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他不是种族主义者。

sentences.en: Is he racist?
sentences.zh: 他是种族主义者吗？

sentences.en: Not raciSt.
sentences.zh: 不是种族主义者。

sentences.en: Not massively overtly racist, I wouldn't have said.
sentences.zh: 我不会说他有非常明显的种族主义倾向。

sentences.en: But I mean, maybe some Portuguese listeners will know more about this than me.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，也许有些葡萄牙听众比我更了解这一点。

sentences.en: But I don't think the racism...
sentences.zh: 但我不认为种族主义……

sentences.en: I mean, he's not...
sentences.zh: 我是说，他不是……

sentences.en: So, for example, he's not overtly anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，他并没有明显的反犹太主义倾向。

sentences.en: And people often said in the 1930s and 1940s,
sentences.zh: 而且人们在20世纪30年代和40年代经常说，

sentences.en: Portugal is unusual in having so little anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙很特别，几乎没有什么反犹太主义。

sentences.en: Now, actually, Franco, I would say, was much more anti-Semitic than Salazar was.
sentences.zh: 现在，实际上，我会说佛朗哥比萨拉查更反犹。

sentences.en: Well, I think that there was this tradition in Portugal of regretting the fact that the Jewish population had gone to Amsterdam and feeling that they'd really, they'd been robbed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为葡萄牙有一种传统，就是为犹太人口流向阿姆斯特丹而感到遗憾，觉得他们真的，他们被洗劫了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, that had been a terrible mistake, a kind of hankering, I suppose, for what might have been.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是个可怕的错误，我想，这是一种对可能发生之事的渴望。

sentences.en: So perhaps that's something that feeds into it.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这就是其中的原因之一。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Tom, have you been converted to Lucifilia?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你被“里斯本情结”转化了吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我已经转化了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And of our Odyssey?
sentences.zh: 那我们的奥德赛之旅呢？

sentences.en: I completely have.
sentences.zh: 我完全被转化了。

sentences.en: I really want to go to Lisbon now.
sentences.zh: 我现在真的很想去里斯本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Oh, Lisbon's a fantastic city.
sentences.zh: 哦，里斯本是一座梦幻般的城市。

sentences.en: Absolutely stunning city.
sentences.zh: 绝对令人惊叹的城市。

sentences.en: One of the top...
sentences.zh: 位列……

sentences.en: So there are four great cities, as you know, in Europe.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，欧洲有四大伟大城市。

sentences.en: There is Lisbon, as I told you the other day, Lisbon, Vienna, Stockholm, and Wolverhampton.
sentences.zh: 正如我前几天告诉你的，是里斯本、维也纳、斯德哥尔摩和伍尔弗汉普顿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Two of them, effectively, Portuguese cities, actually, these days.
sentences.zh: 其中两个，实际上，如今已是葡萄牙城市了。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Wolverhampton.
sentences.zh: 伍尔弗汉普顿。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I will go, because obviously, you know, as I said, I associate Portugal with sunburn to my buttocks.
sentences.zh: 我会去的，因为显然，正如我所说，我把葡萄牙和屁股上的晒伤联系在一起。

sentences.en: Is that the image on which we're really going to end this podcast?
sentences.zh: 我们真的要以这个形象来结束这期播客吗？

sentences.en: I'm prepared to overlook that.
sentences.zh: 我准备忽略这一点。

sentences.en: I feel that you have educated me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你教育了我。

sentences.en: And in fact, to a degree, I've educated myself, because I've really enjoyed reading up.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在某种程度上，我也教育了我自己，因为我真的很享受阅读相关资料的过程。

sentences.en: I like to think we've all been educated, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我愿意相信我们都受到了教育，汤姆。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, we will say adeus to all of you.
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这个重磅消息，我们要向大家说再见了。

sentences.en: You can go off and listen to your Fado music and help yourself to pastes de nata.
sentences.zh: 你们可以去听听法朵音乐，享用一下葡式蛋挞。

sentences.en: And we will return with, I can't even remember what we're doing next week, but it'll be absolutely riveting.
sentences.zh: 我们将带着——我甚至不记得下周要做什么了，但一定会非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: It'll be great, won't it?
sentences.zh: 一定会很棒，不是吗？

sentences.en: It'll be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 一定会很精彩。

sentences.en: It will indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It will indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So enjoy that, and we will see you then.
sentences.zh: 那么尽情享受吧，我们到时候见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余味》。
